title: Monitoring with pg_stat_statements
description: Identify top slow queries, track buffer cache hit ratios, and monitor lock contention with pg_stat_statements.

data.text: **`pg_stat_statements`** is the gold standard extension for tracking query performance. It normalizes query text (replacing literal arguments with `$1`, `$2`), aggregating execution frequency, cumulative duration, and I/O buffer reads across all running queries.

data.title: Finding the Top 5 Most Time-Consuming Queries
data.content: Identifies which queries consume the most CPU and I/O in aggregate.
data.code:
SELECT 
    queryid,
    substring(query, 1, 60) AS short_query,
    calls,
    round(total_exec_time::numeric, 2) AS total_time_ms,
    round(mean_exec_time::numeric, 2) AS avg_time_ms,
    round((100.0 * shared_blks_hit / nullif(shared_blks_hit + shared_blks_read, 0))::numeric, 2) AS cache_hit_pct
FROM pg_stat_statements
ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 5;

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Enable `pg_stat_statements` in `shared_preload_libraries` for all production databases.
Focus optimization efforts on queries with the highest `total_exec_time`.
Target a cache hit ratio of 99%+ on active transactional workloads.
